descripcion: Brewery on the kura street of Saijo, one of Japan's three sake capitals. Fixed the Kamotsuru label in 1873 and opened its first kura as a visitable shop.
Saijo brewery focused on junmai. Its Shusenkan, an early 20th-century wooden house, works as a tasting room and shop.
Brewery founded in 1868 in Akitsu, birthplace of the Hiroshima soft-water fermentation method. Recovered the nearly lost Hattanso rice variety.
Brewery founded in 1880 in Kurose, brewing in short runs and selling mainly through appointed distributors and its own kura shop.
Brewery on the island of Ondo, the first in Japan to make kijoshu, sake fermented with sake instead of water. Own online shop.
Founded in 1907 and the only brewery on the island of Etajima. Its Doki no Sakura label is tied to the island's former naval academy.
Brewery founded in 1871 in Takehara. Its Maboroshi label is brewed with a yeast isolated from apple, unique in the sector.
Brewery founded in 1865 in the Kabe district, north of the city of Hiroshima, focused on everyday junmai.
Brewery founded in 1875 in the Nigata district of Kure, known for the Ugo no Tsuki label. No own website found.
